original_value: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a rapidly evolving technology that is changing almost every business, and aquaculture is no exception. In this work we present an integrated IoT platform for the acquisition of environmental data and the monitoring of aquaculture environments, supported by a real-time communication and processing network. The complete monitoring platform consists of environmental sensors equipped in a swarm of mobile Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) and Buoys, capable of collecting aquatic and outside information, and sending it to a central station where it will be stored and processed. The sensing platform, formed by the USVs and Buoys, are equipped with multi-communication technology: IEEE 802.11n (Wi-Fi) and Bluetooth for short range communication, for mission delegation and the transmission of data collection, and LoRa for periodic report. On the back-end side, supported by FIWARE technology, an interactive web-based platform can be used to define sensing missions and for data visualization. Results on the sensing platform lifetime, mission control and delay processing time are presented to assess the performance of the aquatic monitoring system.

result.paraphrase: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a fast-changing technology reshaping nearly every industry, and aquaculture is no exception. In this work, we introduce an integrated IoT platform for collecting environmental data and monitoring aquaculture environments, backed by a real-time communication and processing network. The full monitoring system comprises environmental sensors mounted on a swarm of mobile Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) and Buoys, able to gather aquatic and external information and transmit it to a central station for storage and processing. The sensing layer, made up of the USVs and Buoys, uses multi-communication technology: IEEE 802.11n (Wi-Fi) and Bluetooth for short-range communication, mission delegation, and data-collection transmission, and LoRa for periodic reporting. On the back end, FIWARE supports an interactive web-based platform for defining sensing missions and visualizing data. Results on sensing-platform lifetime, mission control, and delay processing time are presented to evaluate the performance of the aquatic monitoring system.
